title: The Scale of Exposure
subtitle: Global estimates from peer-reviewed scientific consensus
caveat: Methodological note: The 3.3–3.6 billion vulnerability figure is assessed at the national and sub-national level based on infrastructure, governance, and geography. Vulnerable communities (such as low-income households, unhoused populations, and racialized minorities) also endure acute climate hazards inside wealthy, low-vulnerability nations.

metrics.label: People in Highly Vulnerable Contexts
metrics.description: Between 3.3 and 3.6 billion people live in settings highly vulnerable to climate change—facing 15× higher mortality from floods, droughts, and storms.

metrics.label: At Risk in Low-Elevation Coastal Zones by 2050
metrics.description: More than one billion people living in coastal cities and settlements will be exposed to annual coastal flood risks and storm surges by 2050.

metrics.label: Facing Chronic Water Scarcity at 2°C
metrics.description: Between 800 million and 3 billion people are projected to endure chronic water scarcity if global warming reaches 2.0°C above pre-industrial levels.

metrics.label: Additional Undernourished in Low-Income Nations
metrics.description: Under high warming scenarios (SSP3-7.0), crop yield reductions could leave up to 183 million additional people undernourished by 2050.
